issues.legal_issue: A court considering a challenge to registration of an FIR must allow the investigation to proceed when the FIR prima facie discloses cognizable offences, rather than evaluating disputed evidence or quashing parts of the FIR.
material_facts: Several complaints alleged that multiple persons had conspired to obtain bogus powers of attorney, fraudulently transfer valuable land, and commit related offences.
The complaints and documents led to registration of an FIR alleging several cognizable offences.
The accused sought to quash the FIR under the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction, relying on documents and an alleged settlement whose contents and correctness were disputed.
The High Court examined the factual details at length, quashed the FIR as to some alleged offences, and allowed investigation into the remaining allegations.
The Supreme Court found that the complaints and FIR, read with the material enclosed, prima facie disclosed various cognizable offences and refrained from deciding disputed matters on their merits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment was set aside, the accused persons’ applications to quash the FIR were dismissed, and the entire FIR was left for investigation. The investigation was directed to proceed impartially, in accordance with law, and expeditiously.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 157 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and the High Court’s jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, the threshold question is whether the FIR prima facie discloses a cognizable offence. If it does, the police may investigate and the court should not stop the investigation. At the quashing stage, the court examines the FIR and prima facie material that requires no proof; it must not act as an investigating agency or appellate court by appreciating evidence or drawing its own inferences, particularly where the material is disputed. The Court applied State of West Bengal v. Swapan Kumar Guha, AIR 1982 SC 949, and distinguished the decisions reported at (2015) 11 SCC 730 and (2011) 3 SCC 351 because they concerned complaints brought before a court, not challenges to registration of an FIR.

predicates.fir_quashing_challenge: The accused challenged the registration of an FIR by invoking a court’s jurisdiction to quash it.
predicates.fir_prima_facie_discloses_cognizable_off: The contents of the FIR and accompanying material, considered at face value, disclosed allegations amounting to at least one cognizable offence.
predicates.whole_fir_left_for_investigation: The entire FIR remains for investigation rather than being quashed in part at the threshold.

issues.definition: When an accused challenges an FIR and its contents prima facie disclose a cognizable offence, the whole FIR remains for investigation.
